summary: Corse stands under the national framework of France. No Corse-specific finding on transgender detainees, border checks or hate violence appears in the sources; the national mechanisms documented in the parent record apply on the island unchanged.
tangentialFactors:
The national custody framework that governs trans detainees in Corse's prisons is Article D248 of the Criminal Procedure Code, which mandates separate establishments for men and women, so placement follows the sex inscribed on identity documents and trans women are typically held in men's facilities. As of 1 November 2016, 13 transgender detainees were held across eight establishments in France, most at Fleury-Mérogis.

A BuzzFeed News feature by Rozenn Le Carboulec profiles Paola, an Argentine trans woman transferred to a men's facility in 2014, where she was met with shouts of "We don't want any women here" despite a passport listing her as female, because French law does not recognise her Argentine legal gender for placement purposes. The same reporting documents inconsistent access to treatment and a 2,000-euro symbolic damages award over detention conditions, with the justice minister pressed to amend D248.
localsOnly: The CGLPL opinion of 25 May 2021 on the care of transgender persons in places of deprivation of liberty builds on referrals received since 2010 and a 2010 opinion on transsexual prisoners, covering all places of deprivation of liberty. Inspections cited include Saint-Martin-de-Ré and Toulouse-Seysses prisons and the Toulouse central police station, with evidence from eight transgender women; it documents discrimination, stigmatisation and health and social-care blind spots and recommends policies to combat the discrimination and exclusion they face, referencing law n° 2016-1547 of 18 November 2016 on justice modernisation and prison transfers and the "racism, antisemitism, LGBT and discrimination" referents appointed since 2018. The CGLPL reports persistent serious violations of trans detainees' rights across the prisons it inspected.
outOfScopeNotes: Whether any of the establishments inspected by the CGLPL lie within Corse is not stated in the sources; the inspections cited are on the mainland. No Corse-specific enforcement data on trans detainees, border checks or hate violence is available in the inventory, so the national assessment applies unchanged on the island.
